meanings.note: Standalone casual thanks; followed by ございます (present) or ございました (completed occasion) for polite thanks.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。

meanings.note: Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Auxiliary na-adjective expressing resemblance or conjecture.

examples.trans: It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.text: 彼は忙しいみたいですね。

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.en: what kind of; what sort of
meanings.note: Interrogative prenominal modifier.

examples.text: どんな音楽を聴きますか。
examples.trans: What kind of music do you listen to?

examples.text: どんな仕事をしているんですか。
examples.trans: What kind of work do you do?

meanings.note: Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb.

examples.text: もう少しよく考えてみます。
examples.trans: I'll think about it a little more carefully.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

examples.text: おっさんが考えてることは誰にも読めないんで。
examples.trans: Nobody can ever read what that guy is thinking.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.
So, what was it you wanted to consult me about?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Godan intransitive verb; 黙ってろ! is a rough 'Shut up!'.
I-adjective; after て-form (～てほしい), means 'want someone to do something'.

examples.trans: I want you to come soon.

examples.text: 諦めてほしくないのです。
examples.trans: I don't want you to give up.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Combines どう (how) + いう (say); どういうこと means 'what does this mean?'.

examples.trans: What is the meaning of this?

meanings.note: 分かってる asks or states ongoing understanding; plain past 分かった means 'got it! / I understand'.

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.note: Plural of 俺 (おれ) with pluralizing suffix ら.

examples.text: 分かってます。でも俺らは安心して商売できないんですよ。
examples.trans: I understand. Otherwise we can't do business with peace of mind.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.

examples.text: お前らが池沢とのケンカに勝てる方法が一つある。
examples.trans: There is one way you guys can win your fight against Ikezawa.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Native Japanese counter for general objects and abstract things like reasons.

examples.text: 理由がもう一つあります。
りんごを一つください。

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Signals recognizing someone ('Oh, Toshi!') or letting out a feeling ('Man, I'm hungry').

meanings.note: Subsidiary ichidan verb written in hiragana after て-form (～てみる).

examples.text: 一度食べてみてください。
やってみなければ分かりません。
examples.trans: You won't know unless you try.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

meanings.note: Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
